speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The point I was making really is in parallel with the point the Minister made about the intersection between Western medicine and alternative medicine.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And if we can extract savings from that intersection, I think this will be consistent with watching the fiscal umbers on healthcare going forward.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I want to thank all the officeholders for Health for the very, very helpful responses to all the speeches that had been made.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And you will see that the members in the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) for Health, we have all spoken up because it is a really important initiative for the population health of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are also thinking during enrolment, there could be some incentives – so, there is another chunk there.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That recurrent amount, about half will go to GPs as their service fee, the capitated service fee, for looking after enrolled patients, and another half will be the additional subsidies for residents, including healthpoints, health screening and so on, which will be free.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: One is that my own term here as a Nominated Member of Parliament is limited and will come to an end pretty much soon.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that all of you will continue to engage with healthcare workers on the ground, not just doctors to reflect our view.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Doctors have always felt that we cannot be a union and sometimes, we are marginalised.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: As it is, there are 15,000 doctors in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There are even more nurses around and someone needs to help represent healthcare workers as we forge forward for Healthier SG.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I am so nervous that I have lost my train of thought.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I will email Minister Ong separately about my final point.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: But you have the opportunity to ask it if you can think of it in the next five minutes.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: About the KPIs, one big thing is that, as MOH and various committees talk about KPIs, please remember to involve doctors in the conversation and not be chasing economics – which is more economically viable.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Let doctors advise you on what we think are feasible, medical and clinical KPIs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For MOH, we always err on the side of over-consulting especially our medical experts.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On representing healthcare workers in the Chamber, I think we have NTUC here and they will always champion workers and especially nurses and healthcare workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We had Ms K Thanaletchimi as Nominated Member of Parliament before.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But even we do not have a healthcare worker as a Nominated Member of Parliament, be rest assured NTUC is there and the Minister for Health will be here too.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: First, for the Minister, I would like to clarify that KPIs and targets are not synonymous.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The White Paper already lists many good KPIs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am just asking MOH to take the next step to set targets for each KPI so that all stakeholders can work together towards achieving those targets.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The best practice in performance management is actually to jointly set KPIs and targets with stakeholders – including doctors of course – and then review them regularly and make adjustments if the conditions change.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Because if this is so, then patients will more likely hit their annual withdrawal limit and thereafter, have to co-pay in cash.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, even if MOH cannot remove the annual withdrawal limit now, can it consider increasing it to, let us say $1,000 a year?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I will take the first question and then Senior Minister of State Janil will take the next two.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we are now essentially on the same page.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Yes, they can enrol with polyclinics and we will continue to review the issue of the annual withdrawal limits.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We will have Ms Hazel Poa and then, we will conclude with Mr Liang Eng Hwa.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When he said that there will be no KPIs for family doctors and no clawback, because that would mean that essentially, if I recall correctly, the amount of money that will be paying in service fee is $400 million a year.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does that mean that we will be paying this $400 million a year, with no accountability?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The other half is a service fee to GPs to help us take care of population.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think she just made a statement to say this is not a good spend of money and if you want it to be spent well, give KPIs and targets to the GPs, and if they do not meet, claw back the fees.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In a major effort like this, we want to bring in the GPs to be part of this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Of course, there will be KPIs with targets and we collectively work together to achieve it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the GP level, they will have certain targets as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I do not think we want to treat them like vendors and contractors where if you missed out on a certain KPI, we claw back the fee.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They care about the health of the population as much as we do, maybe more than Members in the Chamber.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Treat them as part of the team, together in the right spirit, we will look at how well we are doing together by reviewing the targets and adjust along the way to achieve good health for Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A billion-dollar set-up, $400 million, if we can keep the population healthy, is money well-spent, even though the Member may think otherwise.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I agree fully there is a real need for that.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But the problem is, like in many of the estates, like my constituency Bukit Panjang, we are running out of void deck spaces to build such centres.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And we need to reserve some of these void deck spaces for other activities like funeral wakes and so on which is also a reality of ageing.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Minister whether would MOH be open to allowing standalone centres, those outside the void decks, which understandably will cost more to build?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But there are some spaces that can actually allow such facility to be built.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And specifically, my question is whether MOH will fund this this facility that is outside the void deck centres which may cost a bit more but, because of the space constraint, we have to do that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It sounds like a specific Bukit Panjang issue which we can discuss.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We always do not say no right at the outset.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We also tend to look at the problem and then we want to solve the problem and the first thing is, we need real estate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I mentioned earlier, if we want to enable ageing in communities, look at what assets is already right in front of us.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And visiting Block 115 in Ang Mo Kio is a bit sobering but it is so inspiring too.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They took back four units or HDB helped take back four units on the second floor.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And in that four units, there is a medical centre, there is a therapy centre, there is a place for them to have activities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Look around our communities, HDB estates are brilliantly built with lots of shared places.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, while we will look at the Member's proposal, let us not close our minds to also the assets that is already right in front of us.
